transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we get into the details of the "Tidal Memory" installation plan for Gallery 4, I want to make sure we go through our usual final check. We've got the draft proposing online-connected playback, eight visitor stations, 15-minute sessions, and a 5:00 PM public opening on October 12. I need to hear from rights, technical, accessibility, and artist representatives — please state any conditions that must be added before I approve this plan. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag several conditions from the music license I reviewed this morning. The countersigned license for Tidal Memory specifies three conditions that must be added to the exhibition plan: first, the installation may only be exhibited through offline local playback — not online-connected playback as the current draft proposes. Second, visitors may not photograph or record the installation. And third, the exact credit line 'Music licensed from Harborlight Editions' must be used. The license arrived after the exhibition packet was circulated, so these conditions haven't been reflected in the draft yet.

The approved headset model supports only six simultaneous stations — not eight as the draft proposes. Additionally, each session must be limited to exactly 12 minutes to prevent thermal shutdown, not 15 minutes as currently planned. The test report is still in the equipment vendor's queue, so this hasn't been reflected in the draft yet.
